analysis.one_liner: Divi's Laboratories manufactures and exports active pharmaceutical ingredients, pharma intermediates and custom-synthesised molecules for global pharma and agrochemical companies, operating mainly as a contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO).
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) results announced in early November 2026: consolidated revenue rose 35.4% YoY to ₹3,676 crore and net profit rose 63.6% YoY to ₹1,127 crore, driven by Custom Synthesis (CDMO) sales up 44% YoY. The stock jumped roughly 15% in two sessions, hit an all-time high near ₹11,786-11,818 and took Divi's past ₹3 trillion market cap for the first time. Management guided double-digit revenue growth for H2 FY27, building on 17% constant-currency growth in H1.
analysis.plain_terms: Divi's makes the chemical building blocks and finished drug ingredients that big pharma companies outsource rather than make themselves. The results were genuinely strong - profit grew faster than revenue because higher-margin custom-manufacturing work is a bigger share of the mix now. The tension: the market has already priced in a lot of future growth - the stock trades near 90 times trailing earnings - so the real question isn't whether the business did well last quarter, it's whether this pace of growth (tied to a handful of large, named manufacturing projects reaching commercial scale) continues for several more years.
analysis.quarters: The available quarterly data (not a fully contiguous run of eight quarters - some quarters were not retrievable and are marked 'Not verified - check on Screener' rather than guessed) shows margin expansion layered on top of revenue growth: Dec 2024 revenue ₹2,604 cr / EBITDA margin ~34.2% / PAT ₹583 cr; Mar 2025 revenue ₹2,831 cr / margin ~33.0% / PAT ₹751 cr; Jun 2025 revenue ₹3,080 cr / margin ~40.7% / PAT ₹902 cr; Sep 2025 revenue ₹2,715 cr / margin ~32.7% / PAT ₹689 cr; Sep 2026 (latest) revenue ₹3,676 cr / margin ~42.6% / PAT ₹1,127 cr. Management attributed the jump to Custom Synthesis growing ~44-50% YoY as three large dedicated projects move through validation, with one nearing commercialisation. No tax or revenue-recognition reclassification was flagged in the results - the EBITDA and PAT trends move together with revenue, so the growth looks like a genuine operating story rather than an accounting artifact.
analysis.performance_read: Divi's has been listed 23.7 years and has gone through three stock splits (5:1 in 2007, 2:1 in 2009, 2:1 in 2015 - a cumulative 20x split-adjustment) but no demergers, so there is no spin-off-related understatement to correct for here. The stock is currently at its all-time high (0% drawdown from peak) after a sharp rally. Despite that, on a relative basis it has lagged its CDMO peer Laurus Labs by a wide margin over longer horizons - 1Y: 73.6% vs peer 145.5%; 3Y: 236.0% vs peer 568.7%; 5Y: 140.8% vs peer 408.1% - while comfortably beating the Nifty over all these periods. Laurus is a smaller, higher-beta stock that re-rated faster off a lower base on similar CDMO optimism; Divi's has been the steadier, larger, less volatile compounder of the two.
analysis.valuation_read: Expensive by conventional yardsticks: ~90x trailing P/E and ~17x price-to-book against an ROE of 16.5%, among the richest multiples in Indian pharma/CDMO. Why it is priced this way: the market is paying up for the CDMO/Custom Synthesis re-acceleration (44-50% YoY segment growth), near-zero debt, 22% ROCE, and optionality around global peptide/GLP-1 outsourcing demand (analysts have flagged Divi's as a possible beneficiary of Novo Nordisk shifting some manufacturing to external partners - this is analyst commentary, not a confirmed contract, and should not be treated as booked business). Whether it is actually cheap is a separate question: at this multiple, the stock is pricing in several more years of sustained double-digit-plus growth and margin durability: any slippage in project timelines would compress the multiple as much as the earnings.
analysis.growth_read: Growth right now is both volume- and margin-led: revenue is up 35% YoY and EBITDA margin has expanded from the low-to-mid 30s into the low 40s (42.6% in the latest quarter) as the higher-margin Custom Synthesis business grew to 62% of H1 sales versus 38% for Generics. That said, this growth has historically been lumpy - Screener-reported 5-year sales growth as low as ~8.7% going into this year, reflecting a period of generic API pricing pressure and project timing gaps. The current acceleration is tied to specific large dedicated projects reaching validation/commercial scale, not broad-based volume growth across the whole portfolio, so durability depends on project-by-project execution rather than market-wide demand.
analysis.health_read: Financially clean: borrowings of only about ₹7 crore as of March 2026, ROCE of 22%, and FY26 operating cash flow of ₹2,738 crore against PAT - a healthy ~105% cash conversion, so profits are turning into real cash, not just accounting earnings. Free cash flow for FY26 was a much smaller ₹221 crore because the company is in a heavy capacity-expansion phase. The thing to watch here is business risk (will the new capacity and the named large projects deliver the volumes guided), not financial risk - there is no leverage or balance-sheet stress to speak of.
analysis.ownership_read: The Divi promoter family has held a stable ~51.9% stake through the last four quarters with zero shares pledged. Institutional ownership is meaningful - domestic institutions around 19.2%, foreign institutions around 5.7% - with the remainder in public/other hands (third-party shareholding breakdowns found did not cleanly sum to 100%, so treat the split between public and 'other' categories as approximate - check Screener for the exact current filing). No single well-known individual investor shows up with a notable disclosed stake; this is a promoter-plus-institution-owned stock, not one associated with a marquee retail investor.
strengths: Custom Synthesis (CDMO) revenue grew ~44% YoY to about ₹2,200 crore in Q2 FY27, lifting that segment to 62% of H1 sales mix
EBITDA margin expanded to 42.6% in the latest quarter from roughly 33% a year earlier as the higher-margin mix scales
Virtually debt-free (~₹7 crore borrowings) with ROCE of 22% and zero promoter pledge
Management has guided double-digit revenue growth for H2 FY27 after 17% constant-currency growth in H1
watchpoints: At ~90x trailing earnings and ~17x book value, the stock already prices in several more years of strong growth - any slip in the 'three large dedicated' Custom Synthesis projects' validation-to-commercialisation timeline would hit both earnings and the multiple

Growth here has historically been lumpy and project-driven rather than steady - 5-year sales growth was reported as low as ~8.7% before this recent acceleration, so one strong year does not yet establish a new sustained trend

Despite the recent rally to an all-time high, Divi's has materially underperformed peer Laurus Labs over 1, 3 and 5 years (e.g., 5Y: 140.8% vs 408.1%), so the re-rating here has lagged peers making similar CDMO bets
The Novo Nordisk/GLP-1 outsourcing angle currently cited by some analysts as a tailwind is speculative commentary, not a signed contract - should not be treated as confirmed future revenue
analysis.one_thing: Whether the three large dedicated Custom Synthesis projects currently in validation actually commercialise on the schedule management guided over the next few quarters - that determines if the current margin and growth re-acceleration (and the ~90x multiple being paid for it) is a durable step-change or a peak.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 headline figures (revenue ~₹3,676 cr, PAT ~₹1,127 cr, growth rates, all-time-high price, ₹3 trillion market cap) were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (Business Standard, Gurufocus, MarketsMojo, Upstox, Screener) and are consistent. Could not verify a fully contiguous 8-quarter trend - gaps are marked rather than filled in. Shareholding percentages (promoter 51.88%, FII 5.71%, DII 19.17%, public 6.55%) did not sum cleanly to 100% across third-party aggregators - treat the non-promoter split as approximate and check the company's latest exchange filing. P/E was cited as ranging 80-90x depending on source and date given the fast-moving price; 89.8x (Screener, most current) was used as primary.
